Internal postmortem for Neerpay (fictional), a Bengaluru UPI bill-payment startup, after a payment outage on 14 September 2026. Facts to use: a release at 19:38 IST changed the retry-limit config of the payment-gateway client and skipped the canary stage; first failed payment 19:42 IST; first customer complaint on support chat 19:51; first alert 19:56 (the only alert watched API 5xx errors, not payment success rate); rollback started 20:21; success rate normal at 20:29; 62,000 payment attempts failed; 214 double-debits auto-reversed by 22:10; 1,240 support tickets; no data lost; security lead confirmed it is not a reportable cyber incident. Actions: canary for config changes (Platform, 30 Sept, PAY-301); payment-success alert (SRE, 25 Sept, PAY-302); runbook rewrite (Payments, 5 Oct, PAY-303); double-debit support macro (Support, 22 Sept, PAY-304); config review checklist (Release manager, 28 Sept, PAY-305). Audience: CTO, engineering leads, head of support. English; 600-900 words; goal: the CTO approves the five actions and owners.

Writer note: Placeholders (facts the brief did not supply): [postmortem authors]; [value of the failed attempts and double-debits, from the payments ledger] (money at risk); [reason the canary was skipped]; [reason for the 25 minutes between first alert and rollback start]; [on-call role and time from the pager log]; and three supporting-information links. All numbers, times and the five actions with owners, dates and tracker IDs are exactly as in the brief. Derived arithmetic, checked: release to first failure 4 min; first failure to first complaint 9 min; to first alert 14 min; first alert to rollback start 25 min; first failure to rollback start 39 min; rollback start to normal 8 min; failed-payment window 19:42-20:29 = 47 min; release to recovery 51 min; recovery to last reversal 1 h 41 min. 14 Sep 2026 is a Monday. Inferences to confirm in the review meeting: the three root causes are drawn from the facts and the actions (the canary and config-review actions imply the process allowed a config change through without either; the alert gap is stated in the brief), and 'the new retry limit reached all payment traffic at once' follows from the canary being skipped. The timeline has 7 entries because only 7 timestamped facts were supplied (the card suggests 8-20); I did not invent events. Language is blameless: no person named as a cause. Notification duties: the brief says the security lead confirmed it is not a reportable cyber incident, recorded in Impact and in 'what went well'. Length about 650 words. Check: --genre genre:incident_report.
samples.text:
Incident: Payment outage after the release of 14 September 2026
Date of incident: Monday 14 September 2026 (all times IST)
Authors: [postmortem authors]
Status: Draft for CTO review

SUMMARY

On 14 September 2026 a release at 19:38 IST changed the retry-limit config of the payment-gateway client and skipped the canary stage. Payments failed from 19:42 to 20:29 IST, 47 minutes. 62,000 payment attempts failed, 214 payments were debited twice, and support received 1,240 tickets. We rolled back the release and success rate was normal at 20:29. All 214 double-debits were auto-reversed by 22:10. No data was lost.

Decision requested: approve the five action items and owners below. The first is due on 22 September.

IMPACT

- Window: 19:42 to 20:29 IST, 47 minutes of failed payments (51 minutes from release to recovery).
- Failed payment attempts: 62,000.
- Double-debits: 214, all auto-reversed by 22:10 IST, 1 hour 41 minutes after recovery.
- Support tickets: 1,240.
- Money at risk: [value of the 62,000 failed attempts and the 214 double-debits, from the payments ledger].
- Not affected: no data was lost. The security lead confirmed this is not a reportable cyber incident.

ROOT CAUSES

1. The release process let a config change skip the canary stage, so the new retry limit reached all payment traffic at once. [Reason the canary was skipped: confirm from the release record.]
2. No review checklist covered config values that govern the payment-gateway client, such as the retry limit.
3. The only alert watched API 5xx errors, not payment success rate. The first customer complaint (19:51) arrived before the first alert (19:56).

TRIGGER

The 19:38 IST release changed the retry-limit config of the payment-gateway client. The first failed payment followed at 19:42.

RESOLUTION AND DETECTION

Resolution: the team rolled back the 19:38 release, starting at 20:21. Payment success rate was normal at 20:29, 8 minutes later. The 214 double-debits were auto-reversed, the last by 22:10.

Detection: a customer reported the failure on support chat at 19:51, 9 minutes after the first failed payment. The first alert fired at 19:56, 14 minutes after it. The monitoring gap is the missing payment-success-rate alert. 25 minutes passed between the first alert and the start of the rollback.

ACTION ITEMS

| Action | Type | Owner | Due | Tracker |
| Create a double-debit reply macro for support | Mitigate | Support | 22 Sep 2026 | PAY-304 |
| Add an alert on payment success rate | Detect | SRE | 25 Sep 2026 | PAY-302 |
| Write a config review checklist | Prevent | Release manager | 28 Sep 2026 | PAY-305 |
| Add a canary stage for config changes | Prevent | Platform | 30 Sep 2026 | PAY-301 |
| Rewrite the payments runbook | Mitigate | Payments | 5 Oct 2026 | PAY-303 |

LESSONS LEARNED

What went well:
- Rollback to normal success rate took 8 minutes.
- Auto-reversal cleared all 214 double-debits without manual work.
- The security lead checked and recorded that this is not a reportable cyber incident.

What went wrong:
- A config change reached production without a canary.
- Customers reported the failure before our own alert did, and the first alert took 14 minutes.
- 25 minutes passed between first alert and rollback start. [Reason: confirm from the chat export; PAY-303 covers the runbook path.]
- Support needed a standard reply for double-debits (PAY-304) and handled 1,240 tickets.

Where we got lucky:
- No data was lost, though no control would have stopped a change that did affect data.
- The alert fired only because API 5xx errors rose. A failure that kept 5xx flat would have had no alert at all.

TIMELINE (14 September 2026, IST)

19:38 Release deployed: retry-limit config of the payment-gateway client changed, canary stage skipped.
19:42 First failed payment.
19:51 First customer complaint on support chat.
19:56 First alert fires (API 5xx errors). On-call paged [confirm role and time from the pager log].
20:21 Rollback of the 19:38 release starts.
20:29 Payment success rate normal.
22:10 All 214 double-debits auto-reversed.

SUPPORTING INFORMATION

Tracker items: PAY-301 to PAY-305.
[Payment success-rate dashboard link]
[Support chat export link]
[Release record for the 19:38 release]

samples.brief:
Media kit text (three pages at most, to be set in a PDF template) for Meher Siddiqui, a Lucknow street-food and home-cooking creator who posts Reels in Hinglish. Use these facts and no others: Instagram 142K followers; average Reel reach 61K over the last 30 days and engagement 5.4% (likes, comments, saves and shares divided by reach), both from Instagram Insights as of 1 Oct 2026; audience 58% women, 71% aged 18-34, top cities Lucknow, Delhi and Kanpur, 83% watch in Hindi or Hinglish; YouTube 28K subscribers. Past work: a 12-outlet Lucknow chaat chain (1 Reel and 3 Stories, 4,100 link clicks); a Kanpur masala brand (2 Reels, 380 orders on her code in 21 days). Testimonial, used with permission: 'Meher's Reel brought us a queue on a Tuesday afternoon.' (Rajiv Tandon, owner of the chaat chain). Rates: Reel Rs 18,000; story set of 3 Rs 6,000; YouTube integration of 60-90 seconds Rs 30,000; 30 days of organic use on the brand's channels included; paid-ad use and whitelisting Rs 9,000 per 30 days; 30-day exclusivity adds 25%; taxes extra; valid to 31 Dec 2026. Contact: meher@example.in, WhatsApp +91 90000 00000. Audience: brand managers at food, kitchen and FMCG brands in North India. English with a light Hinglish line; 250-450 words; goal: a brand manager replies with a brief or a call request.

Writer note: Placeholders: [source and date to add] after the YouTube 28K (the brief gives no source or date for it) and [reply time] in the next step (no response time supplied). Used only the facts in the brief; nothing else about Meher, her content or her brands is claimed. Choices worth checking: (1) the brief states the Insights source and 1 Oct 2026 date for reach and engagement ('both'); I applied the same source and date to the audience split, which should be confirmed against her Insights export. (2) The two past collaborations are described by type because the brief supplies no brand names (chaat chain, 12 outlets; masala brand, Kanpur); the card prefers named brands, so add them if she can share them. (3) The worked example (1 Reel + 1 story set = Rs 24,000; with exclusivity Rs 30,000) is arithmetic on the brief's rates and reads '25%' as applying to the fees quoted; confirm with Meher that exclusivity is priced on the whole package. (4) 'Each price includes 30 days of organic use on the brand's own channels' restates the brief's included-usage line. (5) The disclosure sentence (clear label, Ad or Collaboration, plus Instagram's paid-partnership tag) is the card's required disclosure line using ASCI-permitted label words, and 'turnaround and revision rounds are agreed in the brief' avoids inventing numbers; both are standard commitments Meher should approve. No platform card is named in the brief, so only the genre check was run. About 340 words, within three pages. The Hinglish line is 'Lucknow ki galiyon ka swaad, ghar ki rasoi mein.' Check: --genre genre:influencer_media_kit.
